title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Ticket Delivery, Reserved Hours and Rate Substitution
content:
Three delivery terms stand in the Demand Service Rate Programs beside the rates themselves.

The service ticket delivery figure is the number of business days after a completed call by which the
service ticket is delivered. The reserved hours figure is the technician hours reserved for the customer
each week, 0 where none are reserved. The overtime column states whether the owner's authorisation is
required before overtime labor is worked. The rate substitution column states whether a maintenance
agreement's own labor rate replaces this program's rate for work on covered equipment.

| Program | Service ticket delivered within (business days) | Technician hours reserved each week | Owner's authorisation required before overtime | Maintenance agreement labor rate substitutes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 10 | 0 | Yes | Yes |
| Priority Response Program | 7 | 0 | Yes | Yes |
| Block Hour Service Program | 5 | 0 | Yes | Yes |
| Emergency Response Program | 3 | 0 | No | Yes |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 2 | 0 | No | No |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 2 | 20 | No | No |

*Reading the last two columns.* The four programs from the Time & Material Account through the Emergency
Response Program carry Yes in the rate substitution column; the Critical Facility Response Program and
the Dedicated Technician Program carry No. The overtime column runs the other way: the three lower
programs require the owner's authorisation and the three upper ones do not. Only the Dedicated
Technician Program reserves technician hours, at 20 hours each week.
